beats.narration: Using one password for every site is an open door; here is how managers lock it.
How Password Managers Protect Your Digital Life
Most people reuse passwords, creating a single point of failure that hackers easily exploit.
Your data is scrambled into unreadable text using strong encryption before it ever leaves your device.
The provider holds your encrypted blob, but only you hold the key to unlock it.
The process happens entirely on your machine, ensuring the provider never sees your actual master password.
While no system is perfect, local encryption makes a massive breach virtually useless to attackers.
They use local encryption, hold zero knowledge of your secrets, and eliminate your password reuse habit.
